shortDescription: Installs the configuration taken from a file on a device supported by NAPALM

options.name: archive_file
options.description: File to store backup of running-configuration from device. Configuration will not be retrieved if not set.

options.name: candidate_file
options.description: Store a backup of candidate config from device prior to a commit.

options.name: commit_changes
options.description: If set to True the configuration will be actually merged or replaced. If the set to False, we will not apply the changes, just check and report the diff

options.name: config
options.description: Configuration to load. Either config or config_file is needed.

options.name: config_file
options.description: Path to the file to load the configuration from. Either config or config_file is needed.

options.name: diff_file
options.description: A path to the file where we store the "diff" between the running configuration and the new configuration. If not set the diff between configurations will not be saved.

options.name: get_diffs
options.description: Set to False to not have any diffs generated. Useful if platform does not support commands being used to generate diffs. Note- By default diffs are generated even if the diff_file param is not set.

options.name: hostname
options.description: IP or FQDN of the device you want to connect to

options.name: optional_args
options.description: Dictionary of additional arguments passed to underlying driver

options.name: provider
options.description: Dictionary which acts as a collection of arguments used to define the characteristics of how to connect to the device. Connection arguments can be inferred from inventory and CLI arguments or specified in a provider or specified individually.

options.name: replace_config
options.description: If set to True, the entire configuration on the device will be replaced during the commit. If set to False, we will merge the new config with the existing one.

options.name: timeout
options.description: Time in seconds to wait for the device to respond
